79	#### Tuple-vs-curried interpretation bridges
80	
81	The subuniverse machinery speaks of tuple-indexed operations `(f ^ 𝑨) a`, while
82	group theory speaks of the curried `x ∙ y`, `ε`, `x ⁻¹` of `Group-Op`{.AgdaModule}.
83	The two agree up to the setoid equality: `(f ^ 𝑨) a` applied to an arbitrary tuple
84	`a` equals the curried operation applied to the components of `a`, by congruence of
85	the interpretation (`interp-cong`{.AgdaFunction}).  These three bridges are the only
86	place the mismatch is handled; everything downstream uses them.
87	
88	```agda
89	module _ (𝑮 : Group α ρ) where
90	  private
91	    𝑨 = proj₁ 𝑮
92	    A = 𝕌[ 𝑨 ]
93	
94	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑨 ]  using ( _≈_ )
95	                      renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
96	  open Group-Op 𝑮 using ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; ⁻¹-cong ; idˡ-law )
97	  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝑮 ⟩ᵍᵖ using ( ε⁻¹≈ε )
98	
99	  -- The binary operation on an arbitrary 2-tuple is the curried ∙ of its components.
100	  interp-tuple-∙ : (a : Fin 2 → A) → (∙-Op ^ 𝑨) a ≈ a 0F ∙ a 1F
101	  interp-tuple-∙ a = interp-cong 𝑨 ∙-Op λ { 0F → ≈refl ; 1F → ≈refl }
102	
103	  -- The nullary operation on an arbitrary 0-tuple is the identity element ε.
104	  interp-tuple-ε : (a : Fin 0 → A) → (ε-Op ^ 𝑨) a ≈ ε
105	  interp-tuple-ε a = interp-cong 𝑨 ε-Op λ ()
106	
107	  -- The unary operation on an arbitrary 1-tuple is the curried ⁻¹ of its component.
108	  interp-tuple-⁻¹ : (a : Fin 1 → A) → (⁻¹-Op ^ 𝑨) a ≈ a 0F ⁻¹

110	```

112	#### The curried closure toolkit
113	
114	A subuniverse of the group algebra is closed under each curried operation.  These are
115	definitional consequences of closure under the tuple-indexed operations, because the
116	curried accessors of `Group-Op`{.AgdaModule} are defined by applying the interpreted
117	symbol to a canonical tuple.

119	```agda
120	  module _ (B : Pred A ℓ) (B-sub : B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑨) where

122	    sub-∙-closed : ∀ {x y} → x ∈ B → y ∈ B → x ∙ y ∈ B
123	    sub-∙-closed {x} {y} x∈B y∈B = B-sub ∙-Op (pair x y) im
124	      where
125	      im : (i : Fin 2) → pair x y i ∈ B
126	      im 0F = x∈B
127	      im 1F = y∈B
128	
129	    -- A subuniverse contains the identity element (the nullary operation forces it).
130	    sub-ε-closed : ε ∈ B
131	    sub-ε-closed = B-sub ε-Op (λ ()) (λ ())
132	
133	    -- A subuniverse is closed under the curried inverse.
134	    sub-⁻¹-closed : ∀ {x} → x ∈ B → x ⁻¹ ∈ B
135	    sub-⁻¹-closed {x} x∈B = B-sub ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → x) (λ _ → x∈B)
136	```
137	
138	#### The subgroup predicate
139	
140	`IsSubgroup B` says the predicate `B` cuts out a subgroup: it respects the setoid
141	equality and is a subuniverse of the group algebra.  The record module re-exports the
142	curried closure properties, so `open IsSubgroup H-isSubgroup` puts
143	`∙-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, `ε-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, `⁻¹-closed`{.AgdaFunction}, and
144	`respects`{.AgdaField} in scope for a fixed subgroup.
145	
146	```agda
147	  record IsSubgroup (B : Pred A ℓ) : Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ) where
148	    field
149	      respects       : B Respects _≈_
150	      isSubuniverse  : B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑨
151	
152	    ∙-closed : ∀ {x y} → x ∈ B → y ∈ B → x ∙ y ∈ B
153	    ∙-closed = sub-∙-closed B isSubuniverse
154	
155	    ε-closed : ε ∈ B
156	    ε-closed = sub-ε-closed B isSubuniverse
157	
158	    ⁻¹-closed : ∀ {x} → x ∈ B → x ⁻¹ ∈ B
159	    ⁻¹-closed = sub-⁻¹-closed B isSubuniverse
160	```
161	
162	Conversely, an equality-respecting predicate that is closed under the three curried
163	operations is a subgroup: the tuple-indexed closure required by
164	`Subuniverses`{.AgdaFunction} follows from the curried closure by rewriting along the
165	interpretation bridges (this is the one direction that genuinely *uses*
166	`respects`{.AgdaField}).

168	```agda
169	  mkIsSubgroup : {B : Pred A ℓ}
170	    →  B Respects _≈_
171	    →  (∀ {x y} → x ∈ B → y ∈ B → x ∙ y ∈ B)
172	    →  ε ∈ B
173	    →  (∀ {x} → x ∈ B → x ⁻¹ ∈ B)
174	    →  IsSubgroup B
175	  mkIsSubgroup {B = B} resp ∙-c ε-c ⁻¹-c = record { respects = resp ; isSubuniverse = isSub }
176	    where
177	    isSub : B ∈ Subuniverses 𝑨
178	    isSub ∙-Op   a im = resp (≈sym (interp-tuple-∙ a)) (∙-c (im 0F) (im 1F))
179	    isSub ε-Op   a im = resp (≈sym (interp-tuple-ε a)) ε-c
180	    isSub ⁻¹-Op  a im = resp (≈sym (interp-tuple-⁻¹ a)) (⁻¹-c (im 0F))
181	```
182	
183	#### The type of subgroups
184	
185	A subgroup of `𝑮` at predicate level `ℓ` is a predicate on the carrier together with
186	a proof that it is a subgroup.
187	
188	```agda
189	  Subgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
190	  Subgroup ℓ = Σ[ B ∈ Pred A ℓ ] IsSubgroup B
191	```
192	
193	A **decidable subgroup** bundles a subgroup with a decision procedure for its
194	membership; this is the Layer-D presentation of a subgroup (ADR-008), mirroring how
195	`DecCon`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Finite.Basic][] bundles a
196	congruence with its decider.  Decidability is genuine data here: it cannot be
197	derived from carrier finiteness, since a predicate on a finite carrier need
198	not be decidable.
199	
200	```agda
201	  DecSubgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
202	  DecSubgroup ℓ = Σ[ B ∈ Subgroup ℓ ] (∀ x → Dec (x ∈ proj₁ B))
203	```
204	
205	#### The trivial and full subgroups
206	
207	The trivial subgroup is the ≈-class of the identity, `{ x ∣ x ≈ ε }`; over a setoid
208	carrier the *class*, not the syntactic singleton, is the right notion.  The full
209	subgroup is the whole carrier.
210	
211	```agda
212	  trivialSubgroup : Subgroup ρ
213	  trivialSubgroup = (λ x → x ≈ ε) , mkIsSubgroup resp ∙-c ε-c ⁻¹-c
214	    where
215	    resp : (λ x → x ≈ ε) Respects _≈_
216	    resp x≈y x≈ε = ≈trans (≈sym x≈y) x≈ε
217	
218	    ∙-c : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ ε → y ≈ ε → x ∙ y ≈ ε
219	    ∙-c x≈ε y≈ε = ≈trans (∙-cong x≈ε y≈ε) (idˡ-law ε)
220	
221	    ε-c : ε ≈ ε
222	    ε-c = ≈refl
223	
224	    ⁻¹-c : ∀ {x} → x ≈ ε → x ⁻¹ ≈ ε
225	    ⁻¹-c x≈ε = ≈trans (⁻¹-cong x≈ε) ε⁻¹≈ε
226	
227	  fullSubgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Subgroup ℓ
228	  fullSubgroup ℓ =  (λ _ → Lift ℓ ⊤)
229	                 ,  mkIsSubgroup (λ _ _ → lift tt) (λ _ _ → lift tt) (lift tt) (λ _ → lift tt)
230	```
